newsitem.title: USA: CME pork complex ends higher on higher cash hogs.
newsitem.headline: CME pork complex ends higher on higher cash hogs.

text.p: CME hog and pork belly futures closed higher to sharply higher, largely in reaction to a surprising swift upturn in cash hog prices Thursday at several Midwest markets, traders said.

Meat packers apparently bid higher for hogs to ensure adequate supplies for planned large Saturday slaughter operations. Livestock sources estimated Saturday's hog slaughter would be in the 150,000- to 200,000-head area.

Also encouraging buying of the futures were ideas Hurricane Fran may force temporary shutdowns of packing plants on the U.S. East Coast. Traders said such shutdowns could reduce pork supplies and force cash pork prices higher.

As of 1400 CDT/1900 GMT, the hurricane was about 105 miles southeast of South Carolina and North Carolina. The National Hurricane Center said upon landfall hurricane-force winds may extend 100 miles inland.
USDA reported cash hogs traded steady to $1.00 per cwt higher at Midwest terminal markets and steady in key Iowa locations. Hogs had been expected to trade lower.
Also, cash traders expect $0.50 to $1.00 higher cash prices Friday as meat packers were expected to continue buying hogs for Saturday slaughter operations.
Pork belly traders said much of the buying in that market appeared to be short covering in reaction to the hurricane news and to ideas recent steep declines in futures were overdone.
Hogs closed up 1.000 cent to unchanged with October up the most at 53.650 cents per lb. Pork bellies closed up 1.075 to 0.700 cent with February up the most at 76.925 cents.
